rows.name: underground palette table (World 1-2 / area type 2)
rows.notes: PRG source of the World 1-2 (underground) area palette: 32 bytes at prgRom 0xCEF = CPU $8CEF, 16 BG palettes (4x4) then 16 sprite palettes. Live value read in-area (get_all_palettes): BG0=0F 29 1A 09, BG1=0F 3C 1C 0F, BG2=0F 30 21 1C, BG3=0F 27 17 1C, SPR4=0F 16 27 18, SPR5=0F 1C 36 17, SPR6=0F 16 30 27, SPR7=0F 0C 3C 1C. Reached the area by pausing on the title screen and writing $075F=0 (world 1), $075C=1 (level digit 1-2) and $0760=2 (area index); the loader then used header $9CBC[2]=$C0 -> $074E=2, $074F=0 (black backdrop, blue-teal bricks). FOUND by search_memory prgRom for the 16-byte BG run '0F 29 1A 09 0F 3C 1C 0F 0F 30 21 1C 0F 27 17 1C' (unique at 0xCEF); the 16-byte sprite run '0F 16 27 18 ...' is unique at 0xCFF, immediately after, so the entry is one 32-byte block. PROVEN with trace_writes read on CPU 0x8CEF: the copy loop at PC $8EBB (inside WriteVRAMBuffer, prgRom 0xEBB) read exactly the 32 bytes $8CEF-$8D0E at frame 146 during the level load, and the parallel write trace showed those bytes appearing at PPU $3F00-$3F1F. PROOF by ledgered write: write_memory prgRom 0xCFC (BG palette 3 slot 1) $27 -> $2C (ledger seq 1), reset_emulator + reapply_edits, re-entered World 1-2 (via a level reload), and the screenshot showed the five ? blocks and the HUD coin rendered cyan instead of orange; PPU palette RAM byte $3F0D then read $2C. undo_edit restored $27. (Note: this table is a single occurrence in the 32 KiB PRG.)

rows.name: water palette table (World 2-2 / area type 0)
rows.notes: PRG source of the World 2-2 (underwater) area palette: 32 bytes at prgRom 0xCA7 = CPU $8CA7, 16 BG palettes (4x4) then 16 sprite palettes. Live value read in-area (get_all_palettes): BG0=22 15 12 25 (SRAM slot0 overlays the shared backdrop; the stored slot0 is 0F), BG1=0F 3A 1A 0F, BG2=0F 30 12 0F, BG3=0F 27 12 0F, SPR4=0F 16 27 18, SPR5=0F 10 30 27, SPR6=0F 16 30 27, SPR7=0F 0F 30 10. Reached by pausing on the title screen and writing $075F=1 ($07... world 2), $075C=1 (level digit 2-2) and $0760=2 (area index); the loader used header $9CBC[7]=$01 -> $074E=0 (water), $074F=1. FOUND by search_memory prgRom for the distinctive 16-byte BG run (live bytes) - the live first byte 22 is not in ROM, so the run '15 12 25 0F 3A 1A 0F' matched uniquely at 0xCA8 and '0F 3A 1A 0F 0F 30 12 0F 0F 27 12 0F' at 0xCAB, placing the whole 32-byte block at 0xCA7. This entry is one record of the area-palette table whose records are [3F 00 20] (PPU addr $3F00, 32 bytes) followed by 32 palette bytes and a 00 terminator, repeating every 36 bytes: water 0xCA7, ground 0xCCB, underground 0xCEF, castle 0xD13. PROOF by ledgered write: write_memory prgRom 0xCB1 (BG palette 2 slot 2, the water colour) $12 -> $16 red (ledger seq 1), reset_emulator + reapply_edits, re-entered World 2-2, and the screenshot showed the whole sea turned red; get_pixel_color(128,100) in the water then read $16 red and PPU palette 2 slot 2 read $16. undo_edit restored $12.

rows.name: castle palette table (World 1-4 / area type 3)
rows.notes: PRG source of the World 1-4 (castle) area palette: 32 bytes at prgRom 0xD13 = CPU $8D13, 16 BG palettes (4x4) then 16 sprite palettes. Live value read in-area (get_all_palettes): BG0=0F 30 10 00, BG1=0F 30 10 00, BG2=0F 30 16 00, BG3=0F 27 17 00, SPR4=0F 16 27 18, SPR5=0F 1C 36 17, SPR6=0F 16 30 27, SPR7=0F 00 30 10 (black/white/grey brick castle; BG2 slot2 0x16 red is the lava/fire, BG3 slot1 0x27 orange the firebars). Reached by pausing on the title screen and writing $075F=0 (world 1), $075C=3 (level digit 1-4) and $0760=4 (area index); the loader used header $9CBC[4]=$60 -> $074E=3 (castle), $074F=0, $0750=$60. FOUND by inspection of the same area-palette table found for World 1-2/2-2: records are [3F 00 20] + 32 palette bytes + 00, repeating every 36 bytes (water 0xCA7, ground 0xCCB, underground 0xCEF, castle 0xD13); the castle live BG run '0F 30 10 00 0F 30 10 00 0F 30 16 00 0F 27 17 00' is at 0xD13. PROOF by ledgered write: write_memory prgRom 0xD18 (BG palette 1 slot 1, the brick colour) $30 -> $16 red (ledger seq 1), reset_emulator + reapply_edits, re-entered World 1-4, and the screenshot showed the whole brick floor red; get_pixel_color on a brick read $16 red and PPU palette 1 slot 1 read $16. A first attempt at 0xD14 (BG palette 0 slot 1) was invisible because the bricks use palette 1, so it was undone. undo_edit restored $30.
